summary: Data-retention CRON backend feature tested end-to-end. All 13 backend pytest cases PASSED (auth guard, non-admin 403, admin 200 with structured report, retention math for password_resets/payment_transactions/coach_messages, net_worth_snapshots preservation, orphan sweep on bank_transactions, /status endpoint, regressions on auth/me, networth history, plaid sync). Scheduler startup log 'Retention scheduler started (daily 03:00 UTC)' confirmed in backend.err.log. auth/login regression returns 200.
critical_code_review_comments: retention_service.py cleanly separates each policy with independent try/except so a single failure won't abort the run — good defensive design.
Orphan sweep uses distinct() which is capped at 16MB result by Mongo; for very large collections this could silently miss orphans. Acceptable for current data volume but note for future.
server.py wire-up correctly uses AsyncIOScheduler in UTC with CronTrigger(hour=3, minute=0). Scheduler shutdown wired via @app.on_event('shutdown').
Admin endpoints return the raw retention report; consider filtering the MongoDB _id (none present in generated report so N/A here) — currently clean.
Manual admin trigger intentionally does NOT persist to retention_runs (only the scheduler wrapper does). Behavior matches spec.
seed_data_creation: All seeded rows prefixed with TEST_* markers using the real Alex test user's user_id (fetched via /api/auth/me). Fresh docs are cleaned up post-assertion. Aged docs are deleted by the retention run itself.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Retention test suite lives at /app/backend/tests/test_retention.py — reuse for regression. Uses pymongo (sync) for seeding + requests for HTTP. Requires admin (support@jaleter.com) and regular user (alex+test1@jaleter.app) credentials to be valid.
